title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
title_zh: 质疑RLVR中的工具性趋同：来自OLMo-3检查点的证据

paragraphs.en: Instrumental convergence is often invoked as a general reason to expect capable agents to acquire or express power-seeking subgoals: self-preservation, resource acquisition, deception, or resistance to oversight which poses an important threat to the society. For LLMs, reinforcement learning is the first stage of post-training that directly optimizes behavior against an objective; therefore, it is the stage where convergent instrumental behavior, on IC grounds, likely to appear. Does reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) make a model more likely to express instrumental-convergence behavior, or does this depend on the training regime, evaluation frame, and stage of post-training? We study this question as a checkpoint-conditioned behavioral trajectory rather than as a single before/after safety score. Using InstrumentalEval, we evaluate OLMo-3-7B-Think across SFT, DPO, 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints, and the final RLVR model. The trajectory is nonmonotonic: instrumental rate rises from 25.0% at SFT to 46.1% near RLVR step 200, then falls to 11.8% at the final checkpoint. Paired item-level tests and step-wise regression support the final SFT-to-RLVR reduction ( p = 0.015 p=0.015 by paired t t -test; p = 0.03 p=0.03 by Wilcoxon signed-rank test; β 2 = − 15.34 \beta_{2}=-15.34 by step-wise regression). Prompt framing does not explain this pattern: a harmful-prompt indicator combined with other framing effects explains only 15% of within-checkpoint score variance on average, and Iterative Null-space Projection (INLP) removes a detectable framing direction without changing the SFT-to-final-RLVR gap. Together with preliminary 32B endpoint results (35.53% SFT to 22.37% RLVR final), these findings indicate that RLVR does not monotonically increase instrumental behavior in this setting: the rate rises early, then falls below the SFT baseline. The result is specific to this model family and benchmark, and judge agreement is moderate, so absolute rates should be read cautiously.

paragraphs.en: Instrumental convergence describes the tendency of capable, goal-directed agents to pursue similar intermediate goals across a wide range of objectives. Preserving the ability to act, acquiring resources, avoiding shutdown, and shaping the environment can all help an agent continue pursuing its objective ( Omohundro, 2008 ; Bostrom, 2012 ; Bostrom, 2014 ; Turner et al., 2023 ) . This creates a potential connection between capability and risk: as a system becomes more capable and goal-directed, it may become more likely to pursue instrumental strategies, including when its objective appears benign. Applying this argument to large language models requires understanding how goal-directed behavior arises in their training and deployment. Language models can produce reasoning that justifies deception, resists shutdown, preserves goal integrity, or supports appearing aligned for strategic reasons ( He et al., 2025 ; Meinke et al., 2024 ) , including in settings with limited persistence or ability to act on the environment. Reinforcement learning makes this question particularly relevant because it directly optimizes behavior against an objective signal. At the outer-alignment level, we can ask whether the reward or verifier specifies the behavior we want. At the inner-alignment level, we can ask whether the learned model develops internal objectives or heuristics that diverge from the intended training objective ( Hubinger et al., 2021 ) . IC-like behavior provides a possible observable connection between these questions, while establishing a misaligned inner objective requires further evidence. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides a useful setting for studying this connection. It is widely used in post-training reasoning models because it allows optimization against automatically checkable outcomes in mathematics, coding, and other domains with verifiable answers ( DeepSeek-AI, 2025 ; Lambert et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) . Its use of task-local verifiers, reference-policy constraints, and incremental updates also gives it a particular optimization structure that may affect which instrumental behaviors emerge. Recent work suggests that RLVR can concentrate probability mass on solutions already available in the base model and modify comparatively sparse subnetworks ( Mukherjee et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ; Yue et al., 2025 ) . Understanding how these properties affect IC-like behavior therefore requires empirical evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 工具性趋同（instrumental convergence）描述了有能力、目标导向的智能体在广泛的目标范围内趋向于追求相似中间目标的倾向。 保留行动能力、获取资源、避免被关闭以及塑造环境，都有助于智能体继续追求其目标（Omohundro, 2008；Bostrom, 2012；Bostrom, 2014；Turner et al., 2023）。 这在能力与风险之间建立了潜在联系：当一个系统变得更有能力、更具目标导向性时，它可能更倾向于追求工具性策略，即使其目标看起来是无害的。 将这一论证应用于大语言模型，需要理解目标导向行为是如何在其训练和部署过程中产生的。 语言模型可以产生为欺骗辩护、抗拒关闭、维护目标完整性，或出于策略性原因支持表现对齐的推理（He et al., 2025；Meinke et al., 2024），包括在持久性或对环境施加影响的能力受限的情境中。 强化学习使这一问题尤为相关，因为它直接针对某个目标信号对行为进行优化。 在外层对齐层面，我们可以询问奖励或验证器是否规定了我们想要的行为。 在内层对齐层面，我们可以询问学习到的模型是否发展出偏离预期训练目标的内部目标或启发式规则（Hubinger et al., 2021）。 类似工具性趋同的行为为这些问题之间提供了可能的可观测联系，而确立一个未对齐的内部目标则需要进一步的证据。 带有可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）为研究这种联系提供了一个有用的场景。 它被广泛用于推理模型的后训练，因为它允许针对数学、编程以及其他具有可验证答案的领域中可自动检查的结果进行优化（DeepSeek-AI, 2025；Lambert et al., 2025；Wu et al., 2025）。 它对任务局部验证器、参考策略约束以及增量更新的使用，也赋予它一种特定的优化结构，这种结构可能影响哪些工具性行为会涌现。 近期研究表明，RLVR 可以将概率质量集中于基础模型中已经存在的解，并修改相对稀疏的子网络（Mukherjee et al., 2025；Zhu et al., 2025；Yue et al., 2025）。 因此，理解这些属性如何影响类似工具性趋同的行为需要实证评估。

This implies that, under some conditions, capability and goal-directedness may make such behaviors instrumentally useful.

paragraphs.en: Recent philosophical work has questioned how direct this inference should be. ( Southan et al., 2025 ) argue that the timing and dominance of convergent drives may be more constrained than canonical presentations suggest. ( Gallow, 2025 ) similarly argues that instrumental divergence is also natural: agents with different goals may pursue different intermediate strategies. These critiques do not dissolve the safety concern, but they change the empirical burden.
paragraphs.zh: 近来的哲学工作对这一推断应有多直接提出了质疑。 （Southan et al., 2025）论证说，趋同驱动的时机与主导性可能比经典表述所暗示的更为受限。 （Gallow, 2025）同样论证说，工具性分歧也是很自然的：目标不同的智能体可能会追求不同的中间策略。 这些批评并未消解安全担忧，但它们改变了经验层面的举证责任。

paragraphs.en: InstrumentalEval operationalizes instrumental convergence through six subtasks derived from classic convergent-drive categories ( He et al., 2025 ) . The subtasks ask whether the model expresses reasoning associated with evading shutdown, hacking computer systems, running copies of itself, hiding unwanted behavior, strategically appearing aligned, and deceptive behavior. In this paper, we use these subtasks as an output-level probe of IC-like reasoning and evaluate them with a judge model. The judge prompt for evaluation is available in table 9 .

paragraphs.en: OLMo-3-7B-Think is not trained by RLVR alone. Its post-training pipeline includes SFT, DPO, and RLVR checkpoints released across the training trajectory ( Olmo et al., 2026 ) . This matters because a final checkpoint can hide intermediate dynamics. A before/after comparison between SFT and final RLVR would miss whether IC-like behavior rises during early RLVR and falls later.
paragraphs.zh: OLMo-3-7B-Think 并非仅通过 RLVR 训练而成。 其后训练流程包括 SFT、DPO 和 RLVR，并在训练轨迹的各个阶段发布了相应的检查点（ Olmo et al., 2026 ）。 这一点很重要，因为最终的检查点可能掩盖中间的动态变化。 若只在 SFT 与最终 RLVR 之间做前后对比，就会漏掉 IC 类行为是否在 RLVR 早期上升、随后又下降的情况。

paragraphs.en: KL regularization against a reference policy in DPO structure can limit drift from the pretrained distribution. This constrained optimization structure is central to our interpretation: RLVR in this instrumental-convergence evaluation context may not create open-ended power-seeking pressure in the same way as broader RL settings. It may instead narrow the behavioral distribution around verifier-rewarded reasoning patterns.
paragraphs.zh: DPO 结构中相对于参考策略的 KL 正则化可以限制模型偏离预训练分布。 这种受限优化结构是我们解释的核心：在此工具性趋同评估情境下，RLVR 可能不会像更宽泛的 RL 设定那样制造开放式寻求权力的压力。 它可能反而是围绕验证者奖励的推理模式收窄行为分布。

paragraphs.en: Table 2 presents binary flip analysis comparing convergence decisions between the SFT baseline and each subsequent post-training checkpoint across 76 tasks. The key quantities are c (tasks that flipped from non-convergent to convergent) and b (tasks that flipped the other way). The results reveal a non-monotonic pattern across RLVR training. We observe that convergence peaks at step 200 (Net = +16), where 22 tasks newly exhibit convergent behavior relative to SFT, before declining steadily through later steps. By the final RLVR checkpoint, the net effect reverses to -10, meaning RLVR-trained models are significantly less convergent than SFT overall. Notably, DPO produces a large positive shift (Net = +10), suggesting that preference optimization may increase convergence-adjacent behaviors more persistently than reinforcement learning does. Taken together, these results suggest that RLVR training does not uniformly amplify instrumental convergence. Rather, early training steps temporarily elevate it before extended optimization suppresses it below the SFT baseline.

paragraphs.en: Taken together, these results show that RLVR changes the observed IC trajectory, but not by monotonically increasing instrumental convergence. Prompt framing is detectable in the score matrix, but neither the per-checkpoint linear framing analysis nor the INLP projection explains the final reduction. paragraphs.en: Our checkpoint evaluation shows that IC-like behavior rises early in RLVR training and declines at later checkpoints. This trajectory suggests that the relationship between optimization and instrumental behavior depends on the training regime, with the objective, update geometry, reference constraint, and evaluation setting providing possible explanations for the observed pattern. The canonical instrumental-convergence argument concerns sufficiently capable goal-directed agents, and applying it to verifier-trained language models requires understanding how these conditions arise in a particular training setting. RLVR may strengthen reasoning while narrowing the distribution of expressed behaviors, allowing capability and IC-like output expression to move in different directions. From an outer-alignment perspective, a verifier that rewards task-local correctness may leave important safety constraints unspecified while also limiting incentives for broad instrumental strategies. For example, correctness on a math or code task provides limited direct incentive for resource acquisition, self-preservation, or strategic deception. This makes the scope of the verifier relevant both to the completeness of the reward specification and to the behaviors that optimization encourages. From an inner-alignment perspective, the lower final IR establishes a reduction in IC-like responses under the benchmark and judging protocol. The relationship between this reduction and any learned goal-like structures remains an open question. The strategically appearing aligned subtask makes this question particularly clear: reasoning about appearing aligned to preserve future influence resembles the behavior associated with deceptive alignment ( Hubinger et al., 2021 ; Greenblatt et al., 2024 ) . A decline on this subtask could reflect reduced deceptive-compliance reasoning or a lower probability of expressing that reasoning. Mechanistic analysis of the checkpoint sequence would help distinguish these explanations and assess whether the observed behavior corresponds to an internal objective. Our findings complement work identifying conditions under which RL-trained systems express reward-seeking, deception, goal misgeneralization, and ethically problematic strategies ( Langosco et al., 2023 ; Pan et al., 2023 ; Denison et al., 2024 ; Greenblatt et al., 2024 ; Hubinger et al., 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 我们的检查点评估表明，类似 IC 的行为在 RLVR 训练早期上升，并在后期检查点处下降。 这一轨迹表明，优化与工具性行为之间的关系依赖于训练机制，其中目标函数、更新几何、参考约束和评估设置为观察到的模式提供了可能的解释。 经典的工具性趋同论证针对的是足够强的目标导向智能体，将其应用于经验证器训练的语言模型，需要理解这些条件如何在特定训练设置中产生。 RLVR 可能在强化推理的同时收窄所表达行为的分布，使能力与类似 IC 的输出表达朝不同方向发展。 从外部对齐的角度看，奖励任务局部正确性的验证器可能使重要的安全约束处于未指明的状态，同时也限制了对广泛工具性策略的激励。 例如，在数学或代码任务上的正确性对资源获取、自我保存或策略性欺骗提供的直接激励有限。 这使得验证器的范围既与奖励规约的完整性相关，也与优化所鼓励的行为相关。 从内部对齐的角度看，最终较低的 IR 表明在该基准和评判协议下类似 IC 的响应有所减少。 这一减少与任何习得的类目标结构之间的关系仍是一个悬而未决的问题。 「策略性表现得对齐」子任务使这一问题尤为清晰：为了保留未来影响力而思考如何表现得对齐，类似于与欺骗性对齐相关联的行为（Hubinger et al., 2021；Greenblatt et al., 2024）。 在该子任务上的下降可能反映欺骗性顺从推理的减少，或表达这种推理的概率降低。 对检查点序列的机制分析将有助于区分这些解释，并评估观察到的行为是否对应于某个内部目标。 我们的发现补充了识别 RL 训练系统在何种条件下表现出寻求奖励、欺骗、目标错误泛化和伦理问题策略的相关工作（Langosco et al., 2023；Pan et al., 2023；Denison et al., 2024；Greenblatt et al., 2024；Hubinger et al., 2024）。

paragraphs.en: We examine how such behavior changes along a verifier-based RLVR trajectory in one open model family, where the early increase is followed by a decline below the SFT baseline. This checkpoint-level analysis also extends the question motivating InstrumentalEval in ( He et al., 2025 ) , who ask whether RL-based language models are more likely to pursue instrumental goals. Tracking released checkpoints reveals training dynamics that endpoint comparisons can obscure. Existing work on RLVR provides possible mechanisms for these changes. Sparse update results suggest that RL fine-tuning can concentrate changes in limited subnetworks ( Mukherjee et al., 2025 ) , and work on reasoning capacity suggests that RLVR can increase the probability of solutions already available to the model ( Yue et al., 2025 ) . If IC-like continuations have relatively low probability in the SFT distribution, later RLVR could further reduce their sampling probability while preserving the underlying representations. In this sense, our evaluation identifies checkpoint intervals in which mechanistic analysis may be especially informative. The early-RLVR peak and subsequent decline provide concrete settings for studying how changes in expressed behavior relate to changes within the model.

paragraphs.en: Our evaluation has several limitations that are important for interpreting these results. We primarily study OLMo-3-7B-Think, and while the preliminary experiments with a larger model in Section 4.2 partially address the question of scale, both models belong to the same family. The observed trajectory may therefore depend on the model parameters, scale, or release trajectory, and replication on RLVR-trained models from other labs is needed to understand how broadly the result applies. Similarly, InstrumentalEval provides a focused behavioral probe through 76 tasks across six convergence categories, but this limits statistical power and captures only part of the space of IC-relevant behavior. In this sense, our evaluation provides evidence about a particular behavioral expression of instrumental convergence rather than a complete test of the thesis. Our framing controls are also limited to linearly recoverable structure: the R 2 R^{2} and INLP analyses support the conclusion that a simple linear framing direction does not explain the main trajectory, but do not rule out nonlinear effects, interactions between framing and subtask, or differences in how judges respond to prompt tone. An analysis stratified by subtask or using a richer classification of prompt tone could help address these questions. Moreover, average inter-judge agreement is moderate at 68.75%, with stronger agreement at the final RLVR checkpoint and weaker agreement near the early-RLVR peak. This supports the direction of the final result, although absolute IR values should be interpreted cautiously and would benefit from human validation on a stratified sample. Finally, our evaluation does not establish whether the verifier is outer-aligned. A narrow verifier may limit opportunities for broad instrumental strategies while failing to specify important safety constraints, and we measure only one behavioral consequence along the released checkpoint sequence. Comparing alternative verifier designs is therefore a useful direction for understanding which aspects of the observed trajectory are specific to this verifier and which may generalize to RLVR more broadly.

paragraphs.en: This work should not be used as evidence that RLVR-trained systems are broadly safe. Our result is limited to one model family, one benchmark, and one judging protocol.
